clue.text: Piece of furniture, as yet incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: as yet means so far, up to now

explanation.surface: A furniture maker admits a piece is still unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the last letter from SO FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee for two or three people to sit on is a common piece of furniture.

clue.text: Rather natural, conceivably, without a distinctive taste

indicators.note: conceivably signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the suffix -ish means rather or somewhat, as in reddish

indicators.note: without says the letter a is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: natural means real, genuine

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flavour as rather natural but lacking any distinctive taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' removes A from REAL to leave REL; 'conceivably' then rearranges ISH and REL.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive flavour or tang is one sense; a chutney-like condiment is another.

clue.text: Long hold-up heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a hitch is a delay or hold-up

explanation.surface: A long delay ends with someone heading off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is the verb, to yearn; 'heading off' drops the H of HITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or have an urge for it.

clue.text: Conservative rebels in moments of truth

parts.note: rebels as a verb means rises up, revolts

explanation.surface: Conservative MPs rebelling at decisive moments for the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive turning point, when things must go one way or the other, is a moment of truth.

clue.text: Glaswegian, perhaps, given to habitual drinking round clubs

indicators.note: round says the drinking word goes around the club letter

parts.note: sottish describes a sot, a habitual drunkard
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A man from Glasgow who drinks heavily on his rounds of the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow is a city in Scotland; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glasgow native is one example of someone from Scotland.

clue.text: Honest and winning still

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up
still means not moving, standing

explanation.surface: An honest person who is still winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and respectable in character, which is what an honest citizen is.

clue.text: Prediction concerning English players

parts.note: for can mean concerning, as in 'as for me'
the cast are the players in a show

explanation.surface: A tip about which English actors or sportsmen will feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what is expected to happen, such as weather ahead.

clue.text: Offend a female head

parts.note: the head of a queue or procession is its front

explanation.surface: A woman in charge gives offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To insult someone openly is to offend them.

clue.text: Cooked piece following right set of instructions

indicators.note: following says the rearranged word comes after the letter for right
cooked suggests the letters are fiddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dish is cooked by following the correct instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook follows a written method listing ingredients and steps.

clue.text: List of charges resulting from spat about a Republican

indicators.note: about says the quarrel word goes around the next letters

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: Price lists drawn up after a row involving a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of prices or duties payable is a tariff.

clue.text: Pause at these, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they should stop at these points.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver or hold back before acting is to pause.

clue.text: What sales rep wants in embassy?

definitions.meaning: a salesperson wants a large percentage paid on each sale
the diplomatic mission of one Commonwealth country in another

explanation.surface: Asks what a salesman hopes for at an embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Among Commonwealth countries the equivalent of an embassy carries this title.

clue.text: Cold clerical office — that's after wearing a slip

indicators.note: after places the cold and office pieces following wearing and a

parts.note: wearing means in, as in dressed in
a curacy is the office of a curate

explanation.surface: A cold job in the church, assigned to someone in a petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' looks like a garment beside 'wearing', but it means a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error, a mistake or lapse in correctness.

clue.text: Wonderful conjuring tricks

definitions.meaning: illusions performed by a stage magician

explanation.surface: Praise for a magician's act.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as slang praise and as the art of the illusionist.

clue.text: British vessel, sailing ship

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: A British boat described as a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque or bark is a type of sailing ship with three or more masts.

clue.text: Play surprisingly large family put on

indicators.note: put on says, in this down entry, the family word sits on top of the rest

parts.note: kin means family, relatives

indicators.note: surprisingly tells us the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A large family surprisingly stages a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of an old monarch and his three daughters is a famous play.

clue.text: Children's game next to American river

parts.note: tag is a playground chasing game
US means American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: Kids play beside a river in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river of the Iberian peninsula, flowing through Lisbon.

clue.text: Awful bores at university become more realistic

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Dreadful bores at college eventually grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up figuratively is to drop illusions and get serious and realistic.

clue.text: One in lobby nearly manages to get flag down

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the shortened lobby word
nearly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone waiting in a lobby manages to stop a passing car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts HALL to HAL, then I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out or wave to stop a taxi is to hail it.

clue.text: Game of catch, then rest

parts.note: to contract an illness is to catch it
in snooker a bridge is the rest supporting the cue

explanation.surface: A sports game: first catch the ball, then have a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the rest is a cue support also called a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard modern form of the bidding card game is a game played by four.

clue.text: Forest officer in rage after third of fires

indicators.note: after says the rage word follows the picked letter
third of picks the third letter of the following word

parts.note: rage is a synonym of anger

explanation.surface: A forest warden is furious about fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest ranger is employed to patrol and protect woodland.

clue.text: Certainly popular feat

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a deed is a feat, an act of note

explanation.surface: An impressive feat that is certainly popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic adverb meaning truly or certainly.

clue.text: R&A 'links'? Wrong area in country

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out incorrectly

parts.note: R and A gives the letters R and A, the golf body's initials
taken as written

explanation.surface: The R&A, golf's governing body, oversees a links course in some foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews; a links is a seaside golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation in the Indian Ocean, formerly called Ceylon.

clue.text: Stake partly guaranteed

indicators.note: partly says only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A wager that is partly secured.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, the stake put in before the deal is called the ante.

clue.text: Sieve and cooking device, but no opener

indicators.note: no opener says the first letter is missing

parts.note: a griddle is a flat iron plate for cooking

explanation.surface: Kitchen gear: a strainer and a hotplate without a tin opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like a tin opener but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve for soil or gravel is a riddle; to riddle is to sift.

clue.text: Adore unlimited spices

indicators.note: unlimited says the word loses both its ends

parts.note: cloves are spices

explanation.surface: Someone who adores spices without limit.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to be devoted to them deeply.

clue.text: Fix waste pipe at the end

parts.note: scrap is waste material

indicators.note: at the end picks the last letter of pipe

explanation.surface: A plumber fixes the end of a waste pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' is a noun, a predicament, not a repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fix means being in a tight spot or awkward predicament.

clue.text: Chief villain in film may be unbalanced

parts.note: top means chief, foremost
a heavy is a film villain or tough

explanation.surface: The main bad guy in a movie may be mentally unbalanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Overloaded at the upper part and so liable to topple over, out of balance.
